notes.title: Final Push
notes.content:
Okay, I think this is the final stretch for this update, my imagination has been utterly drained over the last year, into the next patch. Adding bespoke, hand crafted, artisnal psychedelic experiences to wander around inside of, based on authentic psychedelic experiences as seen in many of the art works found within A Fool's Art Gallery. The list of things added to this update is so extensive I can't even remember everything and should have probably taken extensive notes, but this isn't what it was intended to be at the start, originally this update was just to add a space relaxation level with some whales flying around. That's in there. But things spiralled out of control, as one does, and extensive amouts of new content ended up being made. Multiple new levels, tons of new NPCs, loads of new art, new music, secret levels, more secret areas, more of everything. Lots more exploration type game play and areas to find and enjoy. The main concept driving this update is player relaxation. 

New levels include:
~Spa and Lounge
~Ocean/Cave/Harbour levels (All connected as one area.)
~Outer space
~The Other Side 
~The Bank/Corporate Hell Maze
~Secret Level in a secret area

New Art:
~More B&W illustrations
~More Existential Esoteric Paintings
~More Street Art
~More Colour Illustrations of various mediums

New NPCS:
~Whales
~Various eye balls
~Shadow Creatures
~Static "Decorative" NPCs based off characters in art works found in A Fool's Art Gallery
~Mr. Bun Bun
~Butterflies
~Additional Geometric 2D and 3D beings from The Other Side
~A bunch of other stuff I can't remember right now

Theres a few more small odds and ends to be tied up, and then a final polish period, and final testing, then it will be ready to unleash.  I don't want to show too many screen shots, because I think it's better to keep things as a surprise, but here is another sneak peek at whats to come.

notes.title: Update: Update.
notes.content:
Hello again, I am still here; things are still progressing. I've had to switch jobs a couple times, and once again find myself unemployed, as is the life of Canadians now; but work on the update has continued and spiralled completely out of control. The goal is to add all the things I wanted to add, but didn't have time/money/etc to add. The external world is more fleshed out, the secrets are bigger and more numerous, the psychedelic set pieces are more trippy, there is even more art now, a bunch of new NPCs. and It is now a full on exploratory type game, on top of it being an art gallery with 20 years of work inside of it. It has officially been in production for over a year now, so that's pretty crazy. I took a couple three months off along the way at various points, due to having to work, and artist's existential issue type stuff, but other than that it's been pretty consistant in how much is being added and worked on.

notes.title: Achievements Question For You
notes.content:
Achievements have been requested a couple times now, and they are something I have wanted to add for increased interaction with the Gallery.

So far I have one option for sure, it's a convoluted process, and fairly technical but I think I can deal with it and get it to work (Fingers crossed); I cannot say if it will be in the next update or when due to this, but it is something I would work on until it's implemented.

I am also trying to get in touch with another GZDOOM dev who has got achievements in their title working, but they are set to private so I cannot outright DM them yet, I might be able to find another way to contact them however.

The method I do have currently at my finger tips logs keystrokes as part of how it registers events for the achievements. 

Therefore my question to you all is:
How do you feel about keystrokes being registered via the app that bridges the GZDOOM engine and Steam's API for achievements?

Is this something you all are okay with, or something you revile and hate? I don't want to impliment it if it will drive everyone bananas. 

I haven't seen any documentation stating it's a dangerous bridge to use, the program is called Steamshim, just so we are all on the same page.

For the moment this appears to be the only way to get GZDOOM to communicate with Steam to enable achievements, unless some wizard out there knows of another way.

Let me know in the comments how you feel about this. 

The update is coming along quite well, and is nearly done and ready for release; I may do the release first and then start working on getting the achievements sorted out just to keep things moving and so the update doesn't get bogged down by technical coding work. 

Also I finally found my thumb drives for getting Linux installed, so at some point the Linux version will be released.

notes.title: I am not dead or homeless.
notes.content:
I got a job, the update is ready for release, to a degree; it was ready for if I ended up becoming a hobo to be released in a finished enough state; however since I now have a job and am returning to a "stable life" (As stable as you can be in Modern Day Canada.) I would like to add some extra spit polishing to the update and make sure it's up to what I would like it to fully be.

There was an AI demo released recently, that is a way better version of what I ultimately would have liked to do with a video game, so that's pretty crazy; given how long it took to produce this update and it's not even half way to that ultimate vision thing, and the AI pumped it out in seconds and it looks photorealistic. Ce la vie.

One aspect of the update is several areas designed for relaxing in, a formerly secret area has been turned into a section of levels with much larger spaces to explore; these areas push the GZDOOM engine to it's utter limits, and provide a space for laid back wandering. Along with two other relaxing area levels, one a plantarium and one a psychedelic experience; along with a bar/lounge area.

A bunch of new art has been added too, in the Pen and Ink/Black and white section, as well as scattered through out some of the new areas. There are also new secrets in the original areas as well as secrets within the new areas to find as well.

A bunch of voxel models have been remade in polygons, smoothing out frame rates in areas that had a bit of chug to them, and a few assets from another game I am making have been added in as props around which add a bit of world building lore to the games I make. They all take place within the same time line. A Fool's Art Gallery is at the start of the time line. When things are stil some what normal.

notes.title: Even More Update
notes.content:
Hello again!

I quit my job because it turned out to be an evil credit usery debt enslavement company, which made me too mad to function at it; I would rather be homeless than make those vampires any cash off the hardwork of Canadian small and medium size businesses. Thankfully most of the people I contacted expressed a deep contempt and distrust of all electronic payment systems and stated their business is cash only. You make me proud, angry Canadians. Keep on raging. You deserve it. So am looking for a job again; this manic shifting of life patterns is disrupting game development a bit, but not bringing it to a halt. 

Since my game is self published, I don't have anyone lording over me pushing for a rushed released deadline. So please put up with my artistic nature. 

On that note, everyone emailing my publisher (Me) about how offended you are, please note I have recieved your complaints about me, and will be firing me immediately. However I willl be rehiring me after we resolve the issue in HR (Also me.), and conclude this tragic affair of cultural offence. After long negotiations with the artist (Me.), our corporation (Me.), has decided we cannot alter the artistic vision or dilute the message. We have however fired HR because no one likes them.

The general next big update is more or less completed, however one additional level I wanted to add to the Spa and Lounge Section is not done. This level breaks the GZDOOM engine completely. It's fantastic. For the last year or so I thought this glitch had to do with my graphics card, or the BSP Node builder (A program that produces information about the map for the engine to read) settings/choice of BSP builder were wrong, along with a whole lot of technical hoopla. 

A big thanks goes out to GZDOOM forum member Enjay, for testing an example map I posted, we were able to figure out it's the engine itself bonking out and not anything on the user end. From this I was able to dig up some very hidden on Google limits within the GZDOOM engine, and from these limits I have figured out how to create the map as desired. It's a sort of puzzle with geometry, draw distance limitations, some black magic, and a lot of testing and retesting. GZDOOM can do vast open spaces, more or less, but not to the maximum map size. 

The limitation is a sort of blessing in a way, because my other project involves a lot of wide open type maps, but simply having every level be a giant open box is honestly pretty boring and dumb. These limitations allow for big open areas, but also demand a creative use of space to get the full effective range of area within the engine, leading to some pretty strange transition area geometry.  It will be worth the wait, I am not promising some cultural paradigm shifting content here like Starfield or Cyberpunk 2077, but it is something I feel you will enjoy for a relaxing space as the world burns around you.

There are also a couple new models from my next game in this update buzzing around and parked on the side of the road. 

This is the graphics glitch being sorted out: The walls should be solid, but as you can see it is not.

notes.title: Update on the update
notes.content:
I am not dead. 
I secured a job, so won't be homeless yet. (Knock on wood.) Althogh I secretly fantasize about having no choice but to go walking through the woods living in a godly fashiuon with the birbs, like a weird wandering wizard hermit guy, and grow a big long shaggy beard for animals to live in. 

First of all before update news, a big thank you to everyone who has bought A Fool's Art Gallery, it was a kind of risky game to build and launch because it doesn't really fit into any catagories. There was some self doubt along the way about the whole thing, but the communities reaction to it has assauged any irrational fears I had about this all. The few refunds that have come in were due to performance issues, being offended, and being bored; all of which have been and are being further addressed, other than the offended one, because I can't help them with that, that's their problem... lol. 

The update is coming along very well, and despite getting completely out of hand, has managed to get even more completely out of hand. One thing leads to another, you know how it is.  What started out as "adding some space whales" has turned into 4 levels/areas to experience, a spa/lounge area, outer space with the planets, a bunch of their moons, and some space ships, for the space whales to fly around, a level of oceanic relaxation, and a level where you can go see God. 

The lounge music is the toughest part of all this, with real instruments it's fairly straight forward to bring an idea in my head out into the physical world, but with the digital tools I am working with, doing so is proving tricky; I have used digital tools to make tons of music, but those were all songs that grew out of the tools themselves, never songs I had in my head that I tried to transpose into the digital format. I am happy with what I have got so far for it, but might change things up a bit before release. No, I don't want to "Get AI to do it" or "Use Fiver". My games are made by me. Every part of them. Every single pixel, bit, byte, etc is a reflection and birthed of myself and my experience. From my brain into the realm of the physical. I don't care if "Michelangelo used assistance". 

Also in this update is the replacement of all voxel models with polygon models for increased performance, the shrinkage of sprites for freeing up VRAM and increasing frame rates on ultra low end systems, more relaxing pictures to look at, and a couple weird new NPCs that have nothing to do with Space Whales or Oceanic Atmospheres.

This update will bring A Fool's Art Gallery from "An Art Gallery with some psychedelic elements" to "An Art Gallery With Digital Psychedelic Experiences", crafted by a guy who has had plenty of them, for anyone who would like to get an idea of what these experiences are like.

The GZDOOM engine is proving to be the perfect little work horse for what I am doing, thankfully the Doom engine was one of my favorite things to play around with as a kid, as I have never been able to get the hang of Unity or Unreal, despite having no problems switching to the Quake 2 and Half Life engines way back in the day when that was a thing, even back then I couldn't get into Unreal editing. With GZDOOM I am able to create some very cool effects and set pieces, and have them operate in a way that is pretty close to what I have seen. Obviously it will never be excatly the same, but it's pretty good how it does come out. These elements are sort of 3D paintings the user can move though independently. What you have seen in my paintings, you can now experience virtually. And this concept deeply interests me, so that future updates will include more and more of these 'paintings come to virtual life' type set pieces.

On a totally unrelated note, my second game is coming together very well, it's got a nice tight game play loop, and some really fun combat elements. It's completely over the top in it's own way, and kind of hilarious to play so far. It keeps distracting me in a good way when I am testing it out. Once enough elements for it have been built, I will be launching a Steam page with a demo.  If I can figure it out, I am considering giving people who purchased A Fool's Art Gallery a discount on the future title. So that's not set in stone, but is something I would like to do.  It is nothing like A Fool's Art Gallery, I try to make something different everytime I make art, and try not to repeatedly make the "same" thing. So the same goes for my video games. Although all my games have a cyber punk vibe to them, it's a reflection of the world I grew up in, a messy technologically driven mad house.


"WHEN is the update coming out?"

Sooner than later, it was originally planned for an early January release, but the sheer volume of content that I am adding kept building, and despite it seeming like an infinite number of things to add, I know there is a certain point where it will all click properly, and I will know it is ready. It's almost there, once it's there it will be unleased upon this world right and proper. 

I hope it totally blows your mind.

notes.title: Æsthetic Update
notes.content:
This is not the next update as planned; it's a massive over haul of the assets.

While looking into optimizations to get the frame rate hammered out even more, it became apparent I had saved ... A lot... Of the Sprites and textures I made at 300 DPI; an old habit from back when we used to print pictures on paper. This game development thing all began as an experiment in if my style and animation could translate into 3d at all; and I think I planned on reducing the DPI later, or assumed the GZDOOM engine forced image files into 72 DPI, but it does not. So. I went through everything, reduced everything to 72 dpi, some textures were 700+ DPI for some insane reason, don't ask me, I have no idea why. Ask someone else.  People on lower end machines should see a much smoother game play experience and improved frame rate. There will still be some hiccups, as A Fool's Art Gallery uses a lot more textures than a typical game, each picture being a unique texture, so getting all that info through the pipeline is it's own little thing to be constantly working on. By reducing the DPI of sprites and textures about 30 megs of raw data was trimmed from the over all file package, and freed up from the video RAM.  

It also adds brightmaps and Titles, bringing a bit of bang to different areas, and sees some incorrect textures corrected. The Titles are small areas of light in front of mostly the paintings, which print the title of the picture at the top corner of the screen. I am still working out how to get this to behave properly but for now it does the job pretty good, if not a bit over enthusiastically. 

Along the way I found a couple images that some how were missed during the construction phase, their title cards are in game, but the images are not; they are in the next update which is the planned update.

notes.title: Tiny Light Update
notes.content:
The update with some new content was taking longer than expected, so this update adds the rotating light at the Light House secret area, it adds a lot to the over all atmosphere so I wanted to get it out ASAP. Normally I don't do tiny updates like this, but It's for the aesthetic. GZDoom doesn't really do "rotating lights"; and I accidentally finally figured out how to assemble what I was looking to do; so none of this was really planned. The next update is a honker though with a new level added for the first '3d painting'. These '3d paintings' are themes I enjoy exploring with my normal paintings etc, and are being added as a "Spa Area for the Mind". So each one is it's own level sort of thing, and working to make a 3d environment to experience akin to what I make in 2D normally.  A Fool's Art Gallery was released in a "Finished State"; but having a video game I can add things to in an abstract way is too tempting to not tinker around with, which is what these '3d paintings' are all about.

I also started working on my 2nd game, which preempts my original plans with what had been my 1st game, and now became my 2nd game, but is now my 3rd game planned for release, while this new 2nd game is planned to be the next release, and Fool's Art Gallery remains as my first game released.

Each game is set in the same universe/world sort of thing; but each one is in a different time period of that world. A Fool's Art Gallery represents the world as it was during a time of peace, on the cusp of something new; the 2nd game is the time that leads to what the 3rd game is set in. The 2nd and 3rd games are more traditional in the sense that you have guns and bombs etc, things/people exploding everywheres, etc. 

I have a cozy little system in place that allows me to work on all 3 games at the same time in a way, but also lets me focus on each one as it needs to be properly focused on.

notes.title: Texture Optimizations
notes.content:
Optimized the hell out of almost all the textures that needed to be; this improves performance on lower end machines and frees up video RAM for future content expansion. Because the Gallery is made up of so many unique textures, one for each piece; it's a bit of a different beast to handle than a 'regular' game and the amount of textures you will deal with there.  Optimized some graphics settings too. 

This afternoon I finally figured out why Windows 10 and probably 11 were launching with absolute garbage graphics settings and no custom keybindings, it was how the command line was set up; it cannot be called from inside the GZDOOM engine like Windows 7, it has to be called externally on boot, but HAS to be from inside the Steam command line functions, and not via an Autoexec, etc method as is the usual mode of doing things. 

So that's part of this patch but also not technically part of this patch. I still consider this version 1. I don't know if there are any laws or rules I have to follow with that, but getting everything ironed out for performance etc is more backend. Blah blah blah. I will actually increase the version numbers as new art etc is added.

notes.title: *#$&ing Windows 10... And Probably 11
notes.content:
Update:
Fixed it finally this evening, Win 10 calls up the config file differently than Win 7, and via Steam it has to be set up ON Steam, not ON or in or part of the actual boot up files/called from inside the game. So now Windows 10 and probably 11 users will start up with the actual proper default graphics settings and custom controls, which allow flight and 3rd person view.

======================================================

Today I got my hands on a very low end Windows 10 machine to test my games on etc to ensure max compatibility. Upon firing up the Art Gallery, it quickly became apparent Windows 10 users are NOT getting the correct default settings and key bindings. Windows 10, and probably 11; are some how over riding the games settings and creating a GZDOOM folder in Documents/My Games/GZDOOM with the most terrible default settings possible and no custom keybindings.

I spent all day trying different fixes, and for some reason none of them are working other than a janky shortcut method, which I am not sure will work once uploaded to Steam, since everyone has different installation paths etc. I think I found a solution, which I am going to try tomorrow. 

For now, if you are running Windows 10, or 11, look in your Fool's Art Gallery folder, copy GZDOOM_Portable.ini to your Documents/My Games/GZDOOM; and rename it to simply GZDOOM. This will set you up with the proper default bare minimum graphic settings, for how the game should look; and also the proper key bindings allowing you to fly and use the 3rd person camera for whatever reason that you might want to do that.

My hugest apologies to Windows 10 and 11 users, first for having to use those OS's, and second for all this BS. On my Windows 7 machine the .ini file works fine. So I had no idea it was even an issue. But alas, Windows 10 (And probably 11); my old nemesis; strikes once again. Never to let me rest. Always pursuing me. Always reminding me of Windows 7 and that it was a functional OS, some how.

This all comes on top of an actual massive update that won't actually change anything from your point of view other than some frame rate hitches on lower end machines, with textures being insanely optimized; and frees up video RAM for future expansions of content. 

I've been in contact with the GZDOOM engine folks, and they told me that flushing the video RAM between levels is not possible, at the moment; but adding the functionality is on their To Do List. So until they To Do List that, I had to find a solution that works now. I am looking at optimizing them further, but for the time being what's been done is working really well. 

Once this Windows 10 and possibly 11 nightmare is fixed, I am going to get the demo launched and proceed onward with whatever the future holds.

Thank you for your support everyone that has played around in my Gallery so far, and for your patience with getting the final kinks and bugs sorted out.

notes.title: Game Crashing Bug Has Been Fixed
notes.content:
UPDATE:
Small patch again tonight, because I optimized the default graphics settings, and also forgot to delete the AutoExec out of the files for Steam on the main release.

Also, it's the anisotropic filtering, not antialiasing, that was turned down, and texture filtering was reduced to linear, instead of trilinear. Basically if you have above 1 gb of gddr3 video RAM, you can probably turn these settings up without crashing the GZDOOM engine.


==============================

The single bug/error that I know of in the game, that I know of, stressing that part here; has been fixed. It was definitly being caused by the texture filtering and AA set up and my potato PC simply not having the VRAM required for such things with the games texture sizes. So now the config file is updated to run on potato PCs universally, while retaining the aesthetic of the vision. If you costomize your display you can back up "GZDoom_portable" so future updates do not replace your settings. Simply delete any updated config file and replace it with your saved one. 

I also deleted the autoexec file because it's job was to launch the specific iWad file running A Fool's Art Gallery, but that is already being done in the pack file, so was causing an error of no specific consequences, but frame rate seemed to improve a bit, so there is that.

And also I don't know when, or how, but the Steam game launch was configured wrong for X period of time, that is now sorted out; as is the same issue for the German version.

So you can now walk around as long as you want, everywhere, forever, without your game crashing, in theory. If this is simply not true, or you find any other issues, please report them in the game error/glitch forum, I want to make sure my game(s) all run properly for everyone. One of the reasons for choosing the GZDOOM engine was it's universal nature. On that note a Linux distribution is planned for the future, I just have to set up a Linux drive on my PC and get the files all sorted out for Steam. All my current Linux devices are Raspberry Pis.  I have to do this soon anyway, as Windows 7 is being dropped and I hate Windows 10/11, so must evolve to Linux. Windows 7 will still be my work OS just because so many software packages I use run on it already, but over time I am sure Linux will slowly replace it entirely. 

I am probably making the German trailer later today, and need to get that up; and then also am planning the Psychedelic Trailer showing some of the environments more.

And as for future updates and content, I got some pretty crazy ideas planned; right now I am cleaning up some animation which will probably be the first major update, and need to scan and colour the full cat animation (50 frames of hand drawn cat walk cycle.) which I think will be the first major update's center piece. 

For example seen below; Corporate Lady, NPCs are getting full shading and highlighting and final touches before variants are then made too. Corporate Lady was the very first NPC I tried animating in the GZDOOM engine in this quest to make a video game, so her animation is a bit less refined that I would like; so in a far, far far, far, far future update I am probably going to redraw her from scratch.

notes.title: A Fool's Art Gallery Release!
notes.content:
UPDATE:
The German censored files keep downloading in the International files place, so Steam and I are working on things, while I break everything even more while waiting. THANK YOU GERMANY FOR PROTECTING US ALL FROM THE EIGHT STICKS ARRANGED IN A SPIRAL SHAPE. 

UPDATE UPDATE:
Okay, it looks like things are set up properly, or I am about to release a video game that gets me arrested in Germany because the files are all confused, IDK; I know the files on the International version are working properly though. I had wanted a Thursday or Friday release, but Saturday will be the day of release now, hopefully in accordance with the cool Saturn god and not the uncool one. I am putting it off to maximize the time in the new release featured section, and trying to hit it right around the daily roll over time. I don't know if this matters or not, because there are 30 games released on Steam on any given day, and a Halloween sale happening as well; not the best time; but it's make or break time here at my one man studio.

If the German version doesn't launch properly, please tell me in the bugs forum. I had to give the files their own unique name to get around Steam smashing them all together for some reason. It SHOULD work, if it doesn't work; then my bad, give me a minute to fix it.

So 9 or 10 AM, Saturday morning, October 28th, 2023; I will publish my first video game, unless something further happens, IDKWTF it could be, but you never know with this all. Knock on wood. 

============================================

So it's finally here. Release day. I just have to do one final check to make sure things are working before hitting the publish button.

There is ONE game crashing bug that I have been able to recreate. I am currently trying to find very specific details about it from crash logs; but what I believe it is caused by is my 10+ year old video card; and from what I can tell it only happens when I speed run through the entire game in one single shot, whereby it then quits to the desktop. From other rare posts about this crash I have found, this issue doesn't happen on higher end more modern machines. HOWEVER if you do experience it, first; let me know in the bug forum, along with your hardware specs. Second; the game autosaves at the start of each level; simply boot back up into the game and start from that level again, it will have cleared the video ram and will run properly again. It might also be my specific video card, and the specific version of GZDOOM.  

And while the game isn't intended to be run through all at once without actually looking at anything along the way; I am sure someone out there will do this, and will crash the game; and hopefully will file a bug report in the community forums.

BESIDES THAT; I would like to say: This is version 1.0. It is what I consider "The Core" of A Fool's Art Gallery. I had to pick a specific point to say "This is when the game will release"; as if I went with an "early access" style release it would be in early access for 50 years. Even now I had to stop myself from adding more content, just to ensure getting the game out the door and get the public launch done.

This core goes up to about 2020, there is tons more art to add, and finish, and will be made in the future. The NPCs you see are a mixture of made specifically for A Fool's Art Gallery, as well as NPCs from another game I am working on. As time goes on, NPCs from my other titles will see their way into a Fool's Art Gallery also, and more custom NPCs just for A Fool's Art Gallery are planned. 

A Fool's Art Gallery is also a "realistic" project that could be finished by myself in a limited time frame in order to get the wheels turning, in the hope that enough copies sell over time that I can focus 100% on game development, and not split my time between whatever job I have at the given time, transit time, and working on games time.

As the game lay out takes up 4 levels of space, instead of the 1 giant level as originally planned (Due to video RAM limits etc.) this leaves a bunch of empty level slots, I think it can go up to 32, not sure about beyond. But with these empty level slots are a number of worlds that will be experimental works of art in their own right, and very large weird environments to explore and relax in. I would like to over time, make this the weirdest video game that has ever been released.

As for the future of my video game development efforts; I currently have a sci fi FPS well under works, it started out as a cyberpunk genre game, well before the genre blew up into what it is; and because of that I have been steering it away from the typical cyber punk look as of late, and into another direction to seperate it. I also keep wanting to do "some kind of Robinhood/Knights of the Round Table" type FPS game too, but have no idea what that is about. But in the future, as things progress I will be asking the community what they think about different ideas.

Thanks to everyone who supports me and my work, I appreciate it.

notes.title: Launch Day Soon
notes.content:
Howdy doo!

It is almost launch day for A Fool's Art Gallery, and I am very excited and ready to barf.

If you find any problems, glitches, or bugs; please post them in the bugs and glitches forum; so that I may spend days without sleep fixing them. As far as I know nothing is broken, knock on wood. 

Thank you for your support in this endeavour, I look forward to releasing more content, and even more video games in the future; A Fool's Art Gallery is the initial push in the direction after many years of dabbling in modding on my own as a hobby for fun. There will be no paid DLCs, or subscriptions, or microtransactions, because frankly I have no idea how to do that stuff and I don't care for it or want it in my products. 

I hope you enjoy the experience, any feed back is welcome.
